Quality as you go

Ripeness, Brix, readings, yeasts, moisture and water activity.

Plot Where it grows

Step 6 · Note variety and spacing

Under Plants, pick the Species and type or choose the Variety. The app shows what it knows about that variety, with its sources. Add the Planting year (the age is worked out), Plant count, and the Row spacing and Plant spacing: planting density per acre and hectare is worked out from them.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 6

Step 7 · Record soil and how I care for it

Under Soil and soil life: the Soil type, the Texture (feel test), and a tick for each care practice you follow, such as mulch kept on the ground or little digging. Count Earthworms per spadeful if you like. Soil test results are rated against Indian Soil Health Card bands, and inputs applied keep their dates.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 7Guidance, not guarantee

Step 8 · Time backing and fruit drop

Under Flowering, give the Blossom shower date. The app works out when the backing shower is due (15 to 20 days after) and when fruit drop peaks (90 to 120 days after flowering), from CCRI figures. Add each flowering with + Add flowering.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 8Guidance, not guarantee

What it is

Plot and cup gathers the cup scores of green lots and roasts made from this plot, beside your other plots. Over seasons it shows which plots and practices give better cups.

Seen fromEstates and plotsOne coffee, one chain

Step 12 · Compare two ways of caring for plants

On Rows, tap Trials, then ＋ New trial. Name it, choose the block and write your aim. A trial has groups: a Control (left as it is) and one or more Treatments (what you change). Tap ＋ Add a group for more. On each visit you note what you see, and the page shows the groups side by side, with how many plants each figure comes from.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 12

Watch out

Rust is counted on 4 marked branches per plant, and berries on the number you choose under Berry branches marked per plant. Use the same branches on every visit, or the counts cannot be compared.

Seen fromEstates and plotsRecords you can trust

Step 13 · Read how to grow and pick

Crop care gathers tips on plant health, flowering, fruit set, berry borer and harvest, for Arabica, Robusta or Both, at Basic, Intermediate or Advanced level. Each tip names its source, mostly the Coffee Board and CCRI.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 13Guidance, not guarantee

Step 14 · See the year's work, month by month

On Crop care, scroll to Year calendar and open Arabica year or Robusta year. Each is a calendar from the Coffee Board's research institute (CCRI). It lists the work for each part of the year, such as harvest and processing in December to January and manuring before the monsoon in April to May.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 14Guidance, not guarantee

Step 17 · Keep the weather for my plots

Open Weather (an account is needed) and choose a place. Places come from estates and plots with a GPS point. The app fetches daily rain and temperature from a free weather service and tops it up every night; your own rain gauge can be added as a place without GPS.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 17

Harvest The day's picking

Step 6 · Note ripeness and Brix

Under Cherry quality, fill what you know: Ripe %, Under-ripe %, Over-ripe %, Floaters %. For sweetness, tap + Add Brix reading once for each refractometer reading; Average Brix shows with the number of readings and their range.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 6

Tip

Not sure what counts as ripe, or when to pick? The Crop care, harvest link under the weights opens the app's guide to what to pick, when and how, with its sources named.

Seen fromLogging a harvestGuidance, not guarantee

Process run Cherry to green

Step 2

Choose the Pathway: Washed, Natural, a honey, anaerobic, or one of the fermentation-led processes further down. It is required.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 2

Step 4 · Use a ready-made list of steps

Open Start from a ready-made protocol (optional) and pick one, such as Washed arabica, Indian estate (Coffee Board of India). You will see 7 steps added. Fill in times and weights as you go. Each step carries a short guide from that source.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 4Guidance, not guarantee

Step 8 · Take pH, Brix and temperature readings

Under Measurements, tap the measures you want for this step: Temp °C, pH, °Brix, Air °C, Air RH % and others, depending on the step. Each one shows a guide range. Tap + Reading now each time you measure; the time fills in, you type the numbers. With two readings or more, a small chart appears with the guide range shaded.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 8Guidance, not guarantee

Tip

On Now, New then Reading (pH, Brix, temp, photo) picks a live run and takes you to it. Each step also has its own Photo button.

Seen fromProcess runsFinding your way

Step 9 · Ferment with a yeast or starter

In a Fermentation step, choose a method with a yeast or starter, such as With yeast / starter. An Inoculation box opens (inoculation means adding the yeast or starter). Pick the Product and type the Grams used. If you like, add the rehydration water, its temperature and minutes, the price per kg and when it went into the tank. The product's notes, a suggested dose for the kilos in the step and how to rehydrate it come from the maker's published sheets.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 9Guidance, not guarantee

Why it matters

Cup quality is often made or lost in processing. With each run's times, kilos and readings kept, this season's best lot can be set beside last season's. Outturn (green out as a share of cherry in) is worked out once the green weight is known.

Seen fromProcess runsKilos carry forward

Green lot What goes to the roaster

Step 4 · Note moisture and grade

Under Quality, type the Moisture %. With no water activity meter, the app estimates it from moisture (10 to 13% only) and says whether it is good for storage. For robusta it adds that the estimate is rough, because it is worked out from arabica figures. Add Density g/L, Screen size, Grade, Cup score and where it is kept under Storage.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 4Guidance, not guarantee

Step 5 · Add water to reach a target moisture

Open Rehydration (from All features). Type Moisture now, %, Target moisture, % and Batch you want at the end, kg. It shows Weigh out green coffee and Add water. Water in kg is the same as litres. Add it slowly while mixing, then let the coffee rest sealed so it soaks in evenly.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 5Kilos carry forward

Step 9 · Record a sample, sale, count or new moisture

For anything else, add a line. + Moisture is a new moisture reading (every reading is kept, so you can watch it in storage). + Count/move is for after counting or moving bags. + Adjust is for anything else. Fill it in, tap Add line, then Save at the bottom.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 9Kilos carry forward

Why it matters

Moisture and water activity decide how long green coffee keeps. The app's guide aims for 11 to 11.5% for long storage. Above about 11.7%, water activity usually passes 0.61. In a long Cafe Imports study, lots above 0.61 lost more cup score in transit. A reading every few weeks shows a drift while there is time to act.

Seen fromGreen lotsGuidance, not guarantee

Roast Heat and time

Step 4 · Choose what I read

Choose what you read: ET only, BT only or ET + BT, and Celsius °C or Fahrenheit °F. ET is the exhaust or air temperature, BT the bean temperature.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 4

Step 5 · Time the roast

Tap Start at charge. The clock runs at the top of the page and stays in view as you scroll. Pause and Reset are beside it.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 5

Step 6 · Log temperatures as I roast

Below the events are the temperature tiles, one for each degree. When the thermometer reads a number, tap that tile: the reading is kept with the time. A held tap removes a reading. Set the range with Start °C, End °C and Interval °C, then Make tiles.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 6

Step 7 · Mark turning point, first crack and drop

Tap each event as it happens: Turning, Yellow, Maillard, FC (first crack), SC (second crack) and Drop. Each keeps its time and the last temperature. Tap again to move it; hold to remove it.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 7

Tip

Tick Drop guide for a guide to when to drop, worked out from the development time ratio (DTR).

Seen fromRoastingGuidance, not guarantee

What it is

Probe connects a thermometer instead of typing: USB, a TC4 or Artisan-style board, or a Bluetooth thermometer. It works in Chrome or Edge, not on iPhone.

Seen fromRoasting

Step 8 · Finish and keep the roast

Tap Finish. Under Result, type the Roasted weight g and the Final roast colour: total time, development, development % and weight loss work themselves out. Tap Save on device.

Seen fromRoasting, step 8Kilos carry forward

Step 10 · Compare two roasts

In the Roastbook, tap Compare roasts, then tap 2 or 3 roasts and tap Compare to lay their curves side by side.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 10

Step 12 · See the curve and rate of rise

Graph shows the roast now in the timer as a curve, with phases, rate of rise and every reading. CSV and Print / PDF save it.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 12

Step 13 · Record roast colour

Open Colour and tap + New reading. Say what you measured (your roast, bought coffee, a sample), then type what your meter shows. With only a phone photo of ground coffee beside a white card, you get a ballpark roast level and Agtron, with how sure it is.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 13Guidance, not guarantee

Tip

Type every number your meter's screen shows. For meters with no published scale (ColorTrack, Colorette, Neotec), the app learns from your own paired readings. Each reading is shown on the other scales too, and named on three roast charts.

Seen fromRoastingGuidance, not guarantee

Cup Brew, cup and taste

What it is

A brew that names its roast joins the coffee's chain: plot, harvest, run, green lot, roast, cup. Over time you can see which roasts and which recipes gave the cups you liked.

Seen fromBrewing and cuppingOne coffee, one chain

Step 2 · Write down the recipe

Pick the Roast from your Roastbook, or type the Coffee (if not from a roast here). Choose the Method * (V60, AeroPress, espresso, South Indian filter and many more). Then fill what you used: Coffee g, Water g (espresso: yield g), Water °C, Grinder and Grind setting, bloom, total time and pours.

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 2One coffee, one chain

Step 3 · Time the brew

The large clock on the form starts with a tap. Set a Cut-off time and it alarms when the brew should stop.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 3

Step 4 · Note how it tasted

Under Measure, add TDS % and Beverage g if you have a refractometer. Under Taste, give a Rating out of 10 and tap Pick flavour notes for words to describe it.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 4

Step 5 · Get closer to the cup I want

Under Dial in, pick where you want to go: Sweeter, Brighter, Fuller body, Less bitter or Cleaner. Or tell it What stands out in the cup?, such as sour, bitter or thin. It suggests what to change, from published findings and common practice, and Put the plan in Next time keeps the plan with the brew. If the section is not there, tick Show brew tips and dial-in help above it.

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 5Guidance, not guarantee

Tip

Save, and Repeat last copies the recipe into a new brew next time. If you only brew or taste, Now's bottom bar gives you New brew, Repeat last and Brew timer.

Seen fromBrewing and cuppingNothing gets lost

Step 6 · Learn how a brewer works

Brew guide explains each kind of brewer (drip and filter, espresso, moka pot, traditional, cold) at Basic, Intermediate or Advanced level. Its step-by-step guides run a timer and buzz at each step. Protocols are repeatable ways of working: a standard cup, measuring strength, dial-in, freshness, cold brew.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 6Guidance, not guarantee

Step 7 · Mix water to the right temperature

Open Water. Type the Hot water °C, Cold water °C, the Final temp wanted °C and how much you need: it tells you how much of each to pour, by weight or by volume. Below, published brewing-water recipes (such as SCA 68/40) make water from two concentrates.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 7

Step 8 · Run a cupping

Open Cup, the Cupping tab, and tap + Cupping. Choose the Protocol: SCA, Barista Hustle 10, Robusta (CQI Fine Robusta) or Simple. Add each sample with + Add sample, one per roast on the table.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 8

Step 9 · Score the samples

Pour every bowl, then tap Start: the session clock runs. Guided takes you step by step with words for each score; Full form shows everything at once. Switch any time; scores carry over. Save, and the scores show on the roast and its green lot.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 9

Step 10 · Find the likely cause of an off flavour

Under a sample, open Off flavour? Find the likely cause. The notes are grouped by where a fault usually starts: farm and drying, green storage, roasting, after roasting, the brewed coffee and the water. Tap the ones you tasted and the likely cause is shown. The causes follow Ted Lingle, The Coffee Cupper's Handbook (SCAA).

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 10Guidance, not guarantee

Step 11 · Taste roasts blind

The Tests tab holds blind tasting tests. Triangle asks whether anyone can tell them apart. Describe asks what the difference is. Preference asks which people like. There is also palate training that ranks sour, sweet and salt. Tap + Test.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 11Records you can trust

Business People, work, sales, land

Step 11 · Compare one coffee with others

Open Shared spaces (an account is needed). Give the space a Name, and optionally the Coffee (optional) everyone is using, and tap Create space. Invite people by email; each adds a copy of their own brews, roasts, cuppings or process runs, and everyone comments. The owner can turn on a read-only public link.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 11One coffee, one chain

Help Snags and words

What it is

iPhone and Bluetooth. Safari on iPhone cannot talk to Bluetooth or USB devices. For a Bluetooth scale, open the brew page in the Bluefy browser; probes in the Roast timer need Chrome or Edge on Android or a computer. Typing readings works everywhere.

Seen fromWhen something goes wrong, and the words used
